# Opentix -- AI Agent Context

This file describes the ticket management system stored in this directory.
Use it as a reference when reading, creating, or modifying tickets and sprints.

---

## What is Opentix?

Opentix is a git-native ticket management system. All project tickets are stored
as Markdown files inside this `.opentix/` directory. The data lives on the
dedicated `opentix` holder branch and is synced through Git, keeping developer
working branches untouched.

**Conflict-free architecture**: Every data mutation (ticket edit, comment, sprint
update) creates a **new file** rather than modifying an existing one. The current
state is derived by reading the latest file. This eliminates all Git merge conflicts.

---

## Directory Structure

```
.opentix/
├── AGENTS.md              # This file (auto-generated context for AI agents)
├── config.yml             # Project configuration (prefix, statuses, sync settings)
├── team/                  # One Markdown file per team member (filename = email)
│   ├── alice@example.com.md
│   └── bob@example.com.md
├── tickets/               # One folder per ticket
│   └── optx-<random6>/
│       ├── info/          # Append-only ticket versions (latest = source of truth)
│       │   ├── <random6>.md   # v1 (original create)
│       │   └── <random6>.md   # v2 (latest edit)
│       └── comments/      # One file per comment (append-only)
│           ├── <random6>.md   # comment 1
│           └── <random6>.md   # comment 2
├── sprints/               # One folder per sprint
│   └── spr-<random6>/
│       ├── <random6>.md   # v1 (original create)
│       └── <random6>.md   # v2 (latest edit)
└── templates/
    └── default.md         # Default ticket template
```

**Key rules**:
- All filenames (inside folders) are **random 6-char lowercase alphanumeric** strings
- Folder IDs use `<prefix>-<random6>` for tickets, `spr-<random6>` for sprints
- Ticket edits create a **new file** in `info/` -- never overwrite
- Sprint edits create a **new file** in the sprint folder -- never overwrite
- Comments are individual files in `comments/` -- append-only
- Team members are individual files in `team/` -- one `.md` per developer
- `config.yml` remains as a single file (written once at init, rarely changed)
- **No `index.json`**, no `sprints.json`, no `team.yml` -- everything is derived from scanning folders

---

## "Latest File Wins" Resolution

When multiple files exist in a folder (e.g., multiple info versions):

1. Parse all files and read the `updatedAt` field (or equivalent timestamp)
2. Sort **descending** by timestamp
3. If two files have the exact same timestamp (same-millisecond edge case), break tie by **filename** (lexicographic sort, deterministic across all machines)
4. Take the first result -- that is the source of truth

This applies to:
- **Ticket info**: `updatedAt` in YAML frontmatter
- **Sprint versions**: "Date updated" field in H2-section format
- **Comments**: Sorted chronologically (ascending) for display; all are shown

## Ticket Format

Each ticket lives in a folder: `tickets/optx-<random6>/`

### Info File (`tickets/optx-<id>/info/<random6>.md`)

```markdown
---
id: "optx-abc123"
title: "Implement user authentication"
status: backlog
sprint: "spr-def456"
priority: high
assignees:
  - alice
  - bob
labels:
  - auth
  - backend
createdAt: "2025-06-01T10:00:00.000Z"
updatedAt: "2025-06-02T14:30:00.000Z"
createdBy: "alice"
branch: "feat/auth"
linkedCommits:
  - "abc1234"
---

## Description

Implement JWT-based authentication with refresh tokens.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Login endpoint returns JWT + refresh token
- [ ] Middleware validates JWT on protected routes
```

### Comment File (`tickets/optx-<id>/comments/<random6>.md`)

```markdown
### 2025-06-01T10:00:00.000Z | alice

Ticket created.
```

---

## Frontmatter Field Reference

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Yes | Unique ticket ID (`optx-<random6>`). Immutable after creation. |
| `title` | string | Yes | Short summary of the ticket. |
| `status` | string | Yes | Current status. One of: `backlog`, `in-progress`, `review`, `done`, `cancelled`. |
| `sprint` | string | No | Sprint folder ID (e.g., `spr-abc123`). Only sprints with type `sprint` (not `break`) can be assigned. |
| `priority` | string | Yes | One of: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`. |
| `assignees` | string[] | Yes | List of assignee names (can be empty `[]`). |
| `labels` | string[] | Yes | List of labels for categorization (can be empty `[]`). |
| `createdAt` | string | Yes | ISO 8601 timestamp of creation. |
| `updatedAt` | string | Yes | ISO 8601 timestamp of last update. |
| `createdBy` | string | Yes | Git username of the creator. |
| `branch` | string | No | Git branch linked to this ticket. |
| `linkedCommits` | string[] | No | List of commit SHAs related to this ticket. |

---

## Status Workflow

```
backlog -> in-progress -> review -> done -> cancelled
```

Valid statuses for this project: `backlog`, `in-progress`, `review`, `done`, `cancelled`

When moving a ticket to a new status, create a **new info file** with the updated
`status` and `updatedAt` timestamp. Do not modify existing files.

---

## Sprint Format

Each sprint lives in a folder: `sprints/spr-<random6>/`

### Sprint File (`sprints/spr-<id>/<random6>.md`)

```markdown
## Title

Sprint 1

## Start Date

2025-06-01

## End Date

2025-06-14

## Type

sprint

## Date created

2025-06-01T00:00:00.000Z

## Date updated

2025-06-01T12:00:00.000Z
```

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Title | Display label, freely editable. |
| Start Date | Calendar date `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| End Date | Calendar date `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| Type | `sprint` or `break`. Only `sprint` can be assigned to tickets. |
| Date created | ISO timestamp of initial creation (preserved across updates). |
| Date updated | ISO timestamp of this version (used for "latest file wins" ordering). |

**Rules**:
- No overlapping date ranges between sprints.
- `startDate` must be on or before `endDate`.
- A sprint cannot be deleted if any tickets reference it.
- Updates create a **new file** in the sprint folder, never overwrite.

---

## Team Members (`team/`)

Team members are auto-registered when they open the project with Opentix.
Each developer gets their own file in the `team/` directory.

### Team File (`team/<email>.md`)

```markdown
# Alice Johnson
Joined: 2025-06-01T10:00:00.000Z
```

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | Developer's display name (from `git config user.name`). H1 heading. |
| Joined | ISO timestamp of when the developer first joined. |
| Filename | Developer's email (from `git config user.email`), e.g., `alice@example.com.md`. |

**Rules**:
- Each developer writes **only their own file** -- zero conflict risk.
- If a developer changes their `user.name`, the existing file is updated but the `Joined` date is preserved.
- Deduplication is by email (the filename).

## Configuration (`config.yml`)

```yaml
prefix: OPTX
statuses:
  - backlog
  - in-progress
  - review
  - done
  - cancelled
defaultAssignee: null
autoSync: true
syncIntervalSeconds: 60
pushMode: direct
commitStrategy: immediate
commitDebounceSeconds: 5
```

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `prefix` | Ticket ID prefix (e.g., `OPTX`). |
| `statuses` | Ordered list of valid ticket statuses. |
| `defaultAssignee` | Auto-assigned user for new tickets (`null` for none). |
| `autoSync` | Enable background sync with remote. |
| `syncIntervalSeconds` | Interval between automatic syncs. |
| `pushMode` | `direct` (push to `opentix` holder branch) or `branch-pr` (open PR). |
| `commitStrategy` | `immediate` (commit per action) or `debounce` (batch). |
| `commitDebounceSeconds` | Seconds to wait before batching commits. |

## Rules for AI Agents

### Reading Tickets

- Scan `.opentix/tickets/` for ticket folders.
- For each ticket, read all files in `info/` and take the **latest** by `updatedAt`.
- Comments are in `comments/` -- read all and sort chronologically.
- Sprint details are in `.opentix/sprints/` folders.

### Creating Tickets

- **Do not** create ticket files manually. Use the Opentix extension commands.
- If you must create a ticket file:
  - Generate a folder ID: `optx-<random6>` (lowercase alphanumeric).
  - Create `tickets/<folder-id>/info/<random6>.md` with all required frontmatter.
  - Create `tickets/<folder-id>/comments/<random6>.md` with initial "Ticket created." comment.
  - Set `createdAt` and `updatedAt` to the current ISO 8601 timestamp.
  - Set `createdBy` to the git username.

### Modifying Tickets

- Create a **new file** in `info/` with the updated fields -- **never modify existing files**.
- **Always** update the `updatedAt` timestamp when creating a new version.
- **Never** change the `id` or `createdAt` fields.
- Add new comments as new files in `comments/` (never edit existing comment files).

### Referencing Tickets

- Reference tickets by their ID (e.g., `optx-abc123`) in commit messages, comments, and documentation.
- Commit message convention: `opentix: <action> <ID> - <description>`

### Things to Avoid

- **Do not** edit `AGENTS.md` (this file) -- it is auto-generated.
- **Do not** modify existing files -- always create new ones (append-only).
- **Do not** delete a sprint folder if any tickets reference it.
- **Do not** assign a `break`-type sprint to a ticket -- only `sprint`-type entries are valid.
- **Do not** use statuses not listed in `config.yml`.

## Current Ticket Context

Opentix automatically detects the current ticket from your git branch name
(pattern: `optx-<6chars>` in the branch name) and writes the full ticket
context to `CURRENT_TICKET.md` at the repository root.

**Read `CURRENT_TICKET.md` first** before starting any coding task to
understand the requirements, acceptance criteria, and current status of
the ticket you are working on.

If the file is missing or says "No ticket detected", check the branch name
or read tickets directly from `.opentix/tickets/`.

This feature can be disabled in `config.yml` (`aiContext.enabled: false`)
or per-developer via VS Code setting `opentix.aiContext.enabled`.
